newsitem.title: INDIA: Security heavy for Miss World crowning in India.
newsitem.headline: Security heavy for Miss World crowning in India.

text.p: The Miss World beauty pageant neared its crowning moment in India on Saturday amid a huge security alert while a squad of would-be suicide protesters kept one step ahead of police.
"It is a most bizarre situation," Julia Morley, the Miss World organiser, said.

Police in this southern Indian city say they have detained more than 100 young activists to head off trouble, but none was from the group of 15 women who have threatened to burn themselves alive to protest against the show.
Shortly before midnight (1830 GMT) one of the 88 young women contestants will win the Miss World title, marking the end of two fraught weeks beset by protests.
Womens' groups, Hindu nationalists and Communist Party activists have attacked the event, complaining it demeans women and threatens Indian culture.
But the threat of self-immolation by members of Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women) led by Kinay Narayana Shashikala has alarmed the Miss World organisers the most.
Shashikala has gone into hiding since Thursday, but right-wing members of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) say they are in contact with her.
"We are looking for her. We will take her into custody when we track her down," Police Commissioner S.C. Burman said.
One man has already turned himself into a human torch to protest against the pageant being staged in India. But that was last week in Tamil Nadu, hundreds of miles away from Bangalore.
Around two billion television viewers are expected to watch the three-hour show, which will include hundreds of extras plus elephants and a massive Hindu temple stage set.
More than 10,000 security officers, including commando units, have been drafted to guard the show. On Friday a court ruled the armed forces could be used if needed.

The police are also on guard for a hitherto unknown group calling itself the Indian Tigers, which has claimed responsibility for attacks on the Indian organisers of Miss World and two small bomb blasts in which no one was injured.
Shashikala has said her followers will mingle with the 20,000 crowd in Chinnaswamy cricket stadium, the open-air venue for the event, and set fire to themselves after first taking poison.
Large numbers of police armed with guns and teargas canisters swarmed around the cricket stadium, and 150 mobile patrols scoured the city for signs of trouble.
Pramila Nesargi, a state legislator, said she plans a "Miss Poverty, Miss Illiteracy" pageant outside the stadium this evening.
